rationale: Same governing concept appears once as an event provenance trace and once as a fuller reference document; the event explicitly links to the reference. Shared IDs are intentional cross-role lineage here, not interchangeable files.

Both paths have identical SHA-256 and identical content. Git history shows the governance-path source was registered on 2026-09-13 and the reference-vault copy was recovered on 2026-09-28. The governance path is the operational source candidate; the reference-vault path is a preserved mirror candidate. Neither has inbound/outbound links in the audited graph, so final canonical promotion is not claimed.

The two files are byte-identical and share Production ID. Git history shows the operational architecture file was added on 2026-09-13 and the Reference Vault copy was recovered on 2026-09-28. Both have zero inbound/outbound local links in the audited graph, so the operational path is a role-based candidate but exclusive canonical promotion is not claimed.
The event-number decision register describes distinct titles and purposes. These two events have different full identities and Production IDs; the short number is a locator only.
The event-number decision register identifies separate subject matter and Stable IDs. Preserve both events and require full-path references.
The register records distinct event purposes and full Stable IDs. This is a short-number collision, not a single event identity.
The two files concern different architecture concepts and declare distinct identities. Keep both and never resolve by short number alone.
The event-number register treats these as separate events with different goals. Preserve both event records.
Different titles and Stable IDs establish distinct event identities. The shared short number is retained as a historical collision.
The event-number register documents distinct Stable IDs, Production IDs and subject matter. Both records are independent event identities.
The second file explicitly declares itself a superseded/non-canonical correction notice pointing to EVT-0052. Preserve it as a correction artifact, not a second canonical event.

Preserve every path and use full-path/stable identity for future references.

This 2022 Gmail-access-claim event has a distinct full Stable ID and Production ID; it is neither the 2021 master-creation event nor the superseded correction notice. This decision covers only the third path; the existing two-path decision remains preserved.

The source files declare different full Stable IDs, dates and purposes. EVT-0033 is a short locator reused by two distinct governance records; preserve both and resolve references by full path and Stable ID.

The archive-destination file explicitly says it is an appendix, not an independent EVT-0039; the Gmail registration-gap file is the canonical Gmail event, and the 2020 interaction-to-discovery request is separate. Preserve all three roles.
The full titles, dates and declared parent links distinguish the 2020 discovery-architecture output from the 2022 interactive-I/O temporal anchor. The short EVT-0040 token alone is not identity.
The full titles, dates and declared Stable IDs distinguish the 2020 automatic-continuity request from the 2022 UTC input-output living-anchor event. Preserve both.

The first file explicitly marks EVT-0070 as a candidate and identifies a different 0.0 graph request; the second has a distinct Stable ID and Production ID for output-anchor ingestion. Preserve the candidate as a request record, not a canonical duplicate.

One record is a master-reference route correction with a declared Stable ID; the other is an error-governance record with a distinct Error ID and explicitly unverified root cause. Preserve the distinction.

The living-inbox file explicitly declares itself a legacy misnumbered record whose canonical event is EVT-0103; the registration-continuation file is the actual EVT-0093 record. Keep the legacy path as correction provenance.
The evidence TXT is a resolver smoke-test artifact with its own evidence Stable ID; the Markdown file is the canonical EVT-0120 event record. Evidence must not be selected as the event parent.
The event record declares a Stable ID and Production ID; the prompt file is a separate prompt artifact without those event identifiers. Preserve both roles.
